report_meta.title: Packing Time & Motion Study — High Volume
report_meta.subtitle: Halfway Day Sale Period Review

sections.title: Executive Summary
sections.text: Halfway Day Sale packing volume was observed across 17 of 23 Makro stores (77 orders total), with dwell time -- not pack speed -- the dominant execution risk: 36 of 96 dwell records were CRITICAL. Amanzimtoti and Springfield posted the fastest pack times in the banner yet still had 4 of 5 dwell records CRITICAL each, confirming the bottleneck is trolley assignment, not packer performance. Cornubia's 38.7-minute average reflects genuine bulk Sale orders, not a process failure, but it inflates the stated banner average pack time to 7.9 minutes -- roughly 2 minutes above what the other 15 stores actually achieved.

sections.title: High Volume Period Headline — Halfway Day Sale (25 Jun – 1 Jul 2026)

executive_facts.statement: Dwell time, not pack speed, is the dominant Sale-period risk: 36 of 96 dwell records were CRITICAL, while pack times across the 15 non-Cornubia stores stayed within a defensible range.

Amanzimtoti (1.27 min) and Springfield (2.90 min) recorded two of the three fastest pack times in the banner, yet both had 4 of 5 dwell records CRITICAL -- proving the constraint is trolley assignment turnaround, not packer speed.

Carnival and Silverlakes had the worst dwell profiles in the banner -- 5 of 5 and 4 of 4 records CRITICAL respectively, both averaging well over two hours -- indicating packers were not being assigned to trolleys promptly during peak volume at these two stores specifically.

Cornubia's 38.7-minute average pack time is driven by genuine large Halfway Sale bulk orders -- three of five orders showed Product Packing & Scan times far above the banner norm, already confirmed as real bulk transactions rather than data entry errors -- so it should not be reported as a process regression.

The banner average pack time of 7.9 minutes includes Cornubia's bulk-order outlier; excluding it, the other 15 stores averaged 5.7 minutes -- a materially different headline number, and the one that should be used when comparing packer performance rather than order mix.

sections.text: Packing itself held up well under Sale-period load, but trolley dwell -- driven by assignment delays, not packer speed -- is the dominant execution risk this period, concentrated at Carnival, Silverlakes, Bloemfontein, Amanzimtoti and Springfield specifically rather than banner-wide.

sections.title: Pack Time Ranking — All Stores, Fastest to Slowest

executive_facts.statement: The 7 fastest-packing stores all averaged under five minutes per order, while Montague Gardens, Germiston and Bloemfontein (excluding the Cornubia bulk outlier) were the only stores averaging over eight minutes -- a real spread across the banner, not noise.

Strubens Valley and Riversands both improved materially versus the Low Volume baseline while still carrying real dwell risk (25% of records CRITICAL at each) -- pack execution recovered under volume, dwell oversight did not.

Excluding Cornubia's bulk-order outlier, the true banner average pack time is 5.7 minutes, not the 7.9 minutes shown on the headline KPI -- this workbook's own recommendations already call for Cornubia to be reported separately, and the Executive Summary tile should follow that guidance.

sections.title: Dwell Critical Rate — All Stores, Worst to Best

rankings.scope_label: Share of dwell records CRITICAL (>31 min)

executive_facts.statement: Four stores -- Silverlakes, Carnival, Bloemfontein and (post-strip) Gqeberha -- had zero dwell records in the OK band; every logged trolley at these stores sat in WARNING or CRITICAL territory at least once, pointing to a systemic assignment gap rather than isolated incidents.

Crown Mines, Alberton, Cape Gate and Germiston recorded zero CRITICAL dwell records despite all being mid-to-slow on pack time -- proof that pack speed and dwell discipline are managed independently at store level, not the same underlying skill.

sections.title: Data Quality & Methodology Flags
sections.text:
• Silverlakes observation date anomaly — all 4 observations are dated the day after the stated Sale window ends. This has not been previously flagged. Recommend confirming with the store whether this is a genuine late-tail observation or a default/incorrect timestamp before treating Silverlakes' figures as representative of peak Sale conditions.
  • Missing OTD Late-Pick Cross-Check sheet — the consolidated workbook supplied for this analysis contains 7 of the expected 8 sheets; the OTD Late-Pick Cross-Check sheet (validating the TnM sample against the real, full-population HV OTD export) is absent. This may not be the final v2 workbook referenced in the deliverables list.
  • Contaminated source files corrected — Gqeberha, Riversands and Strubens Valley originally contained rows dated within the prior Low Volume period, plus order references duplicated identically across all three files. Contaminated rows were stripped before analysis; Gqeberha is left with only 3 genuine HV observations, so its figures should be treated with caution.
  • Bloemfontein artifact excluded — one dwell reading in the thousands of minutes was identified as a date-rollover data error and excluded from the average.
  • Ottery blank submission — no Observation Log data for the HV period; dwell, exception and behavioural/readiness data exists but there is no pack-time visibility for this store during the Sale.

Before this analysis is finalised into a management report: confirm the Silverlakes observation date, source the missing OTD Late-Pick Cross-Check data, and correct the Executive Summary's banner average to either exclude Cornubia or clearly label it as bulk-order-inclusive -- none of these are process failures, but reporting them uncorrected risks the headline KPI being read as worse than the true packing performance.

provenance.extraction_notes: Pack times converted from the source mm:ss format to decimal minutes for consistency with this system's numeric citation checks; original mm:ss values are preserved in the source documents. The 8-sheet consolidated workbook convention described in the project context brief was not fully present in the uploaded file -- 'OTD Late-Pick Cross-Check' is missing (7 of 8 sheets present) -- so no OTD validation figures are included in this analysis; recommend re-running once the complete workbook is available. Silverlakes' observation dates (all 2026-07-02) fall one day outside the stated Sale window and were not flagged in the source docx or context brief; surfaced here as a new finding. The banner average pack time KPI in the source workbook's Executive Summary sheet (7:53 / 7.883 min) includes Cornubia's bulk-order outlier despite the source docx's own Recommendation 6 stating Cornubia should be 'reported separately from banner averages to avoid skewing the headline KPI' -- both the inclusive and exclusive figures are shown here rather than silently picking one.
